text: A student investigated the effect of acid concentration on the rate of diffusion in agar jelly. The
student was given three test‑tubes containing bromothymol blue indicator in agar jelly.
Bromothymol blue is a blue indicator that turns yellow in the presence of an acid.
The student used this method:
Step 1 label three beakers A1, A2 and A3
Step 2 put 20cm of 1 mol per dm hydrochloric acid solution into beaker A1
Step 3 put 2cm of 1 mol per dm hydrochloric acid solution into beaker A2
Step 4 add 18 cm of distilled water to the hydrochloric acid solution in beaker A2
Step 5 use a clean syringe to transfer 2cm of the solution from beaker A2 to beaker A3
Step 6 add 18 cm of distilled water to beaker A3
Table 1.1 shows the final concentrations of the hydrochloric acid solution in each beaker.
